**Finding re-submitted: compliant (sits at the fallback)** — Rule T4C, Termination for convenience. No redline proposed; document text unchanged.

Repair made: the rationale now expressly records that § 17(b) is an unconditional at-will right despite omitting the words "for convenience," so the failed deterministic check is a phrasing false negative rather than a substantive gap.

Summary of the position:
- **Our exit right (§ 17(b), p0118):** terminate "at any time" on 90 days' written notice, no cause or condition, no early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in the Agreement — within the fallback's 60–90 day band and fee cap.
- **Vendor exit right:** none for convenience; Garman may terminate only on insolvency events or uncured material default (§ 17(c), p0128). Maintenance under § 10 is a renewable one-year term with no Garman walk-away. Walk-away trigger not engaged.
- **Noted, not redlined:** 90 days rather than our preferred 30, and silence on a pro-rata prepaid-fee refund on a § 17(b) termination (refunds arise only on termination for Garman's default). Minor sub-elements; a redline is disproportionate given the penalty-free exit and the perpetual licence structure in § 17(a).
